root_causes: Inefficient exploration strategy: the agents continued generic Explore actions in the kitchen and bathroom even after all three target objects were localized on the kitchen table, wasting several steps (e.g., steps 11–14).

Suboptimal task allocation and waiting: one agent frequently executed Wait while still holding an object already at the goal or while the other agent was moving an object (e.g., step 21 and 26–28), underutilizing available parallelism.

Replanning inertia around Rearrange actions: repeated Rearrange commands were issued for objects already effectively being transported toward the bench, indicating conservative or redundant replanning (steps 15–18 and 26–28).

Lack of completion-aware termination of manipulations: at the end, both cup_0 and toy_food_2 remained in-hand rather than clearly placed despite success being registered, suggesting the policy optimizes for proposition satisfaction without explicitly cleaning up grasp states.
improvement_suggestions: Add a state check before issuing Explore: once all task objects have known poses, switch from exploration to direct pick-and-place planning and prohibit further Explore actions for that episode unless an object becomes unknown.

Improve multi-agent coordination by explicitly assigning disjoint object goals and minimizing Wait actions: e.g., each agent should be responsible for specific objects or regions, and should not remain idle while holding an object that still needs to be placed.

Refine the Rearrange planning logic to avoid repeated commands on the same object unless a precondition has changed; use progress-aware thresholds to stop reissuing the same Rearrange when the object is already en route or successfully placed.
Introduce a post-condition that objects must be both on the target receptacle and not in any agent’s hand to count as fully placed, and add a short ‘release/cleanup’ phase before ending the episode.

Incorporate a cost-aware planner that penalizes unnecessary navigation and waiting time more strongly, encouraging more direct paths from object locations (kitchen table) to the bench and better utilization of both agents.
overall_assessment: The task was ultimately completed successfully, but the trajectory contained notable inefficiencies in exploration, redundant replanning, and underuse of the second agent. Execution quality is solid in terms of correctness but only moderate in terms of efficiency.
task_instruction: Put the mug, squeezer, and toy food on the bench in the entryway.
